home.guide_p1: Start from how much privacy you need and how comfortable you are with wallets. A decentralised exchange gives the most control and anonymity; an exchange with a no-KYC tier is easier and has deeper liquidity.
home.guide_p2: Look at trading fees, spreads and network fees together rather than the headline fee. Check that the coins and networks you need are supported, and that the platform has a clear history and answers when something goes wrong.
home.guide_p3: Make a small test deposit, trade and withdrawal before committing larger amounts. Spread counterparty risk across platforms and keep long-term holdings in self-custody.
home.guide_p4: Use a hardware or well-audited software wallet, check URLs and contract addresses, grant wallet permissions only when needed and avoid large custodial balances. No-KYC does not remove your legal or tax obligations, and it reduces your recourse if something goes wrong.
home.ad_p: Your tile carries a Sponsored label, reaches people who already avoid KYC, and leaves the directory order untouched. We review every advertiser first.
faq: Know Your Customer is the identity check regulated services run before letting you trade: ID card or passport, proof of address, sometimes a selfie. It exists for anti-money-laundering rules, and it concentrates sensitive data that can leak in a breach.

It depends on where you live. Using a platform that does not ask for ID is legal in most countries, but tax and reporting rules still apply to you. Decentralised protocols face less direct oversight; you stay responsible for following your local law.
What do None, Light and Tiered mean?
None: no ID and no account details. Light: no ID under a stated limit, or only an email or phone number. Tiered: ID is required above a threshold, written on each listing.
Which type of platform is best for beginners?

Start with an exchange that has a no-KYC tier: it works like the apps you know. A decentralised exchange gives the most privacy and control, but you need to be comfortable with a wallet and network fees.

Exchanges have tighter spreads and fast internal transfers. Decentralised exchanges show lower protocol fees but add network costs. Instant swaps build their margin into the quote, and ATMs add a cash-handling markup.

We check each listing against the platform’s documentation and how the app behaves, then review it again over time. If a service removes no-KYC access or makes ID mandatory for its core features, we re-tag or remove it.

Some "Visit" buttons are affiliate links, marked on each platform page. We label every sponsored placement. Neither changes the order of the directory, which is sorted by the identity each platform asks for.
A listing is out of date. How do I report it?
Use the "Report a change" link on the platform’s page, or the one in the footer. We check every report before we update a listing.
